notes: Held-out realistic workflow tasks across 47 tools and six business functions; deterministic final-state scoring. Top official score 42.47% at snapshot. Used as a family prior signal, not as Zapier Agents product performance.
600 public tasks, 100 per business domain. Top public pass rate 50.3% at snapshot. Correlated with private leaderboard; independence must be capped.

Ten off-the-shelf models, expert-derived INCOSE ground truth. Best Anthropic model median recall only 47% with 11% false-flag rate. Relevant primarily to requirements review, not requirement drafting.
User study reports 30–40% reduction in test-development effort; targeted examples improved ROUGE-L up to 30%. Used for family human-time prior, not product success.
Functional correctness 89.69% ACU and 84.00% ASDM; scripts generated for industrial ECU HIL benches. Used as family evidence with transfer discount to vendor products.
Executability 90.33% ACU and 81.31% ASDM. Kept as supporting metric separate from functional correctness.
Industry-deployed RAG HIL assistant outperformed general-purpose LLMs in A/B user study on helpfulness, truthfulness and satisfaction; abstract does not expose enough numeric detail for P(success).
LLM approach on five open-source projects achieves weighted F1 ~0.86 for architecture-doc↔source trace-link recovery; comparable to TransArC 0.87 and above no-SAM baseline 0.62.
243 threats across 15 case studies and >8000 generated threats; 85.4% success mapping threats to MITRE ATT&CK. Subtask evidence only, not full threat-model success.

benchmark: Mintlify State of Knowledge controlled benchmark
notes: Across 2,400 controlled tests on 20 docs sites, accuracy stayed 94–99% across formats; Markdown+llms.txt reduced failed navigation requests from 2.23 to 0.11/task. Generic documentation-structure evidence, not individual product quality.

Nine frontier LLMs on 3,000 de-identified industrial ISO 26262 HARA cases. Best ASIL macro-F1 only 0.261. Kept as a strong cautionary family signal, not converted to P(success) for software safety-impact analysis because the task transfer is material.

126 cases across 9 electronic components and 3 hardware platforms. DeepSeek-R1 reached 55.6% pass@1 with schematic information; cross-platform migration varied strongly by stack, with top MicroPython/Pico 73.8% but best ESP-IDF only 29.4%. Used as a broad embedded-development family prior with task relevance, not as any product's score.
DeepSeek-R1 improved to 65.1% with correct schematics after retrieval/compiler-feedback strategies; support signal showing context/tooling matters, not a generic product success rate.

94,987 release notes from 3,369 repositories across 6 languages; LLMs consistently beat traditional baselines, strongest on tree2sum and still weak on diff2sum. Metric is deliberately non-probability because the paper reports several automated/human quality dimensions rather than one Definition-of-Done pass rate.

Seven embedded designs / 34 datasheets; 97.5% compatibility-verification accuracy and 8.6x input-context reduction. Kept non-probability for broad datasheet analysis/driver tasks because the evaluated task is a narrower deterministic compatibility-verification pipeline.

benchmark: ProReFiCIA industrial requirements change impact analysis
notes: Best LLM+prompt variant achieved 85.7% recall on an unseen industrial dataset; engineers review only 3.0% of all requirements. Very close to req-change-impact DoD but does not alone measure false positives.
With domain knowledge via RAG recall rose to 95.8% while reviewed set increased from 3.0% to 3.4%; retained as supporting upper-bound signal rather than a second independent success observation.

900 generated requirements across o3-mini/DeepSeek R1 and three prompt styles. Median 4/5 for Unambiguity and Verifiability, 5/5 for Singularity; human validation on 50 samples. Quality is not directly converted to P(success).
Public summaries report node F1 around 0.57: current systems identify architecture components materially better than their relations.

Edge F1 around 0.13 in public benchmark summaries; relational reasoning and hallucinated dependencies are dominant failure modes. Used as a conservative success proxy only for architecture-diagram/relationship-heavy tasks.
700 human-validated QA pairs from 20 technical manuals; includes factual, procedural and unanswerable questions. Benchmark infrastructure evidence; model scores not encoded here.

Professional multi-page/multi-document QA up to 2,303 pages, including technical manuals, with human-verified evidence pages and multimodal evidence. Used to justify low confidence in naive long-context priors until per-model scores are ingested.

Specialized French financial documents: text/table 85–90%, charts 34–62%, multi-turn degrades to ~50%. Domain differs from engineering manuals but usefully bounds brittle multi-step document analysis.

Best overall system ~44% accuracy on expert-verified extra-long professional document QA; failed/missing/unparsable count as incorrect. Strong family prior for large-document reasoning, not product-specific evidence.
20 synthetic audit tasks across 8 SOC 2 controls; Claude Sonnet 4.6 led at 82% average. D5 tasks averaged below 28% across models, so this is not evidence that complex compliance judgment is solved.
Real customer data with expert ground truth; Claude Opus 4.6 achieved 86.1% accuracy on whether changes warrant security testing. Vendor-run, so capped at C.

metric: standardized exam gain vs LLM-tutor control
notes: Adaptive LLM tutoring produced +0.15 SD in paper exam performance over access to a generic LLM tutor. Supports value of structured/adaptive tutoring but not a direct task-success probability.
Models excel at historical evidence acquisition but struggle with longitudinal diagnosis and adaptive teaching. Used as a cautionary capability signal, not a probability.

Across four LLMs, traceability accuracy ranged 85.1–88.4%; GPT-4o reached 88.4%. Task links requirements to generated Lustre designs, making it a strong but domain-specific family prior for traceability.

Eight LLMs across four aerospace/healthcare traceability datasets; optimized prompting reached F2 0.70 on validation and state-of-the-art test results. Exact aggregate test score is not exposed in the public abstract, so no P(success) is encoded.

94,987 release notes across 3,369 repositories and six languages. Fine-tuned Ministral-8B tree2sum reached 53.14 ROUGE-L; expert evaluation on 100 outputs scored completeness 4.02/5, clarity 3.68/5, conciseness 3.47/5, organization 4.23/5. Raw diffs performed materially worse. Used as structured-release-note quality evidence, not a direct success probability.

benchmark: Harness State of AI-Driven Software Releases
notes: 500 engineering leaders: 57% still use human-in-the-loop review for every line of AI-generated code and 29% report spending more time on code review than before. Used as a cautionary release/CI effort signal, not P(success).

First industrial automotive HARA benchmark under ISO 26262, 3000 de-identified cases and nine frontier LLMs. Models produce plausible hazard narratives but remain weak at categorical risk assessment; best ASIL macro-F1 0.261. Strong negative prior for autonomous safety impact/risk classification.

Eight commercial/open LLMs on 922 JavaScript vulnerability patches with functional-preservation calibration. Best model fixed 23% under judge-based evaluation; study also demonstrates that LLM-as-judge can overestimate over-fixes.

200 curated real CVEs under uniform token budget and pinned cross-vendor judge panel, mean of three runs; top Claude Opus 5 pass rate 64.3%, pass@3 80.5%. Judge-based and protocol differs from execution-calibrated benchmark, so both are retained rather than averaged as independent ground truth.

benchmark: Smart Evidence Management for Automotive SPICE
notes: Paper states systematic discovery/evaluation of evidence consumes roughly 40–60% of ASPICE assessment preparation time and evaluates a human-AI evidence-management approach. Retained as process/effort evidence; no robust public success probability encoded from the accessible abstract.
